newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power weak amid supply abundance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power weak amid supply abundance.

text.p: Western U.S. spot electricity prices remained weak amid abundant hydroelectric supplies, particulary in northern California, and slow holiday demand, market sources said Monday.
"Prices have come off. There is quite a bit of hydropower," one trader said.

A lack of surplus power offers from the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) through Thursday was discounted amid realization that regional hydroelectric reservoir levels will be above normal after the recent heavy rain and snow.
BPA's withdrawal from the market was attributed to short-term flood control measures at federal hydroelectric projects.
Traders said much of today's business was focused on Thursday, with little demand cited ahead of the New Year holiday on Wednesday.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Thursday was quoted at $13.50-14.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $14.00-15.00 on Friday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Thursday was little changed at $9.00-11.00.
Thursday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was slightly lower at $13.00-$15.00, while off-peak was quoted at $9.50-11.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Thursday was quoted at $13.50-15.00, down from $14.00-18.00 for Monday.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Thursday was quoted near $9.00-10.00 per MWh.
Thursday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were also lower at $13.00-15.00 . Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was down at $9.00-10.00.
